data.title: U.S. drilling rig count flat for second straight week in Baker Hughes survey
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. remained unchanged at 603, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. added 1 to 460 in the week ended October 23, while gas rigs dropped 1 to 132 and rigs categorized as miscellaneous stayed flat at 11.

The total rig count was up by 53, or 9.6%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 40, or 9.5%, from a year ago, and gas rigs gained 11, or 9.1%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin remained unchanged in the past week at 272, while the Eagle Ford gained 2 to 43 and the Williston Basin added 1 to 31.

data.title: Mergers and acquisitions
data.description:
The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 2020 GMT on Friday:

** CVC and Belgian investment firm GBL which this month raised their bid for Italian pharmaceutical group Recordati to €53 a share, had secured a 74.3% stake in the firm by the end of the offer period, a regulatory filing showed.

** Private equity firm Inflexion said on Friday it would sell a majority stake in British testing and safety compliance company Celnor Group to Goldman Sachs Alternatives.

** Chinese state-owned investment group Shanghai International offered to buy a 51% stake in Haitong Unitrust International Financial Leasing for about $1.16 billion, according to a joint statement.

** Spanish soccer club Valencia CF said an investment group backed by KKR co-founders George Roberts and Henry Kravis would buy a 42% stake in the club in a deal valuing it at €1.25 billion ($1.4 billion) including debt.

** BASF has increased its takeover offer for German chemicals manufacturer Evonik Industries to €24 per share, two people close to the deal told Reuters.

** Hong Kong-listed mining and metals company MMG offered on Friday to guarantee the supply of ferronickel to European stainless steel producers, in an effort to address EU antitrust concerns over its $500 million bid for Anglo American's Brazilian nickel business.

** Malteurop, one of the world's largest producers of beer ingredient malt, has acquired Chunlei Malting Co to expand its capacity in China, the French company said.

** Smith & Nephew's talks with Johnson & Johnson to combine with the US group's orthopaedics division fell apart after the London-listed group refused to agree to its former CEO leading the merged business, the Financial Times reported , citing people familiar with the matter.

** Gilead Sciences said on Thursday it will acquire PepStar Therapeutics' oral inflammation drug program, including an experimental bowel disease treatment, for $1.275 billion in cash upfront.

data.title: Raw sugar posts first gain in six sessions as oil rises
data.description:
Raw sugar futures on ICE rose for the first time in the past six sessions as oil prices rallied and El Nino-linked weather concerns persisted, while coffee fell.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar settled up 0.11 cent, or 0.5%, at 20.24 cents per lb after falling for a fifth consecutive session on Thursday to close down 1.6%. The market lost 3% in the week.

* Consumers and traders are likely to have come in on the buy side, seeing good value after the recent falls as there is no shortage of bullish drivers in the market, said consultant Michael McDougall.

* These include excess El Nino-linked rain in top grower Brazil and further gains in energy prices , which can tempt cane mills to lower sugar output and ramp up ethanol fuel production.

* Elsewhere, India has extended the deadline for allowing duty-free ‌imports of 1 million metric tons of raw sugar to December 31 from October 31, giving importers more time to bring in the commodity to the world's biggest sugar-consuming country.

* Sugar prices in India, also the world's second-largest sugar producer, are soaring as the nation experiences lower-than-usual monsoon rains owing to the El Nino weather pattern.

* White sugar rose 0.2% to $534.80 a metric ton, although posting a 3.6% weekly loss.

COFFEE

* Arabica coffee settled down 5 cents, or 1.6%, at $3.0745 per lb​​, having touched a six-week high of $3.1820​ on Wednesday. It gained 0.6% weekly.

* Coffee is being driven by critically low exchange inventories and a strong real , which deters exporters in top grower Brazil from selling dollar-priced coffee by lowering local-currency returns.

* ICE arabica stocks fell again on Friday to 227,978 bags, near the lowest level in 27 years.

* Traders are monitoring this Sunday's presidential election in Brazil, which could cement further gains for the real if opposition candidate Flavio Bolsonaro wins, as polls indicate.

* Robusta coffee fell 1.8% to $3,242 a ton. The robusta market lost 5% in the week.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​​settled up 15 pounds, or 0.3%, to 4,311 pounds per ton, having settled down 3.9% on Thursday.

* New York cocoa was little changed at $5,592 a ton.

* Both markets posted a 1% weekly loss.

Results of Operations

Net Income

Net income was $24.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $2.2 million, or 9.8%, from $22.1 million for the second quarter of 2026. The increase primarily reflected a $4.8 million decrease in income tax expense, including a $4.0 million tax credit benefit, partially offset by a $1.4 million decrease in noninterest income, a $720,000 reduction in the recovery for credit losses, a $483,000 decrease in net interest income, and an $87,000 increase in noninterest expense.  Net income increased by $7.0 million, or 40.7%, compared to $17.3 million for third quarter of 2025.  The year-over-year increase reflected the acquisition of First IC Corporation ("First IC") in the fourth quarter of 2025 and was primarily attributable to a $15.7 million increase in interest income and a decrease in a $2.9 million increase in income tax, offset by a $4.0 million increase in interest expense, a $5.4 million increase in noninterest expenses, a $1.8 million decrease in noninterest income, and a $471,000 reduction in the recovery for credit losses.

Net income was $68.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $18.4 million, or 36.4%, from $50.4 million for same period in 2025. The increase reflected the First IC acquisition in the fourth quarter of 2025, and was primarily attributable to a $37.6 million increase in net interest income and a $1.4 million increase in recovery of credit losses, partially offset by a $18.9 million increase in noninterest expense, an $871,000 decrease in noninterest income and an $885,000 increase in income tax expense.

Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin

Interest income totaled $69.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, down $678,000, or 1.0%, from the previous quarter, primarily due to a $56.2 million decrease in average gross loans. Compared with the third quarter of 2025, interest income increased by $15.7 million, or 29.1%, primarily due to a $766.9 million increase in the average balance of gross loans, a $44.8 million increase in the average balance of investments, and a 33-basis-point increase in loan yield.

Interest expense totaled $26.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $195,000, or 0.7%, from the previous quarter, primarily due to a $27.9 million decrease in average interest-bearing deposits and a $34.8 million decrease in average borrowings. As compared to the third quarter of 2025, interest expense for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $4.0 million, or 17.8%, primarily due to a $562.8 million increase in average interest-bearing deposits balances and offset by a $49.6 million decrease in average borrowing balances and a three-basis point decrease in interest-bearing deposit costs. The Company currently has interest rate derivative agreements totaling $650.0 million that are designated as cash flow hedges of our deposit accounts indexed to the Effective Federal Funds Rate (3.88% as of September 30, 2026). The weighted average pay rate for these interest rate derivatives is 3.38%. During the third quarter of 2026, we recorded a credit to interest expense of $1.5 million from the benefit received on these interest rate derivatives compared to a credit of $1.4 million and $3.8 million recorded during the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively.

The net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 4.07%, compared to 4.11% for the previous quarter, a decrease of four basis points. The yield on average interest-earning assets decreased by five basis points to 6.52% from 6.57%, while the cost of average interest-bearing liabilities remained unchanged at 3.36%. Average interest-earning assets decreased by $54.1 million from the previous quarter, primarily due to a $56.2 million decrease in average loan balances. Average interest-bearing liabilities decreased by $62.8 million, reflecting a $27.9 million decrease in average interest-bearing deposits and a $34.8 million decrease in average borrowings.

As compared to the same period in 2025, the net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 increased by 39 basis points to 4.07% from 3.68%, primarily due to a 28-basis-point increase in the yield on average interest-earning assets of $4.24 billion and a six-basis-point decrease in the cost of average interest-bearing liabilities of $3.09 billion. Average earning assets for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $811.7 million from the third quarter of 2025, due to a $44.8 million increase in average total investments and a $766.9 million increase in average loans. Average interest-bearing liabilities for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $513.1 million from the third quarter of 2025, driven by the increase in average interest-bearing deposits of $562.8 million, offset by a $49.6 million decrease in average borrowings.

Noninterest Income

Noninterest income for third quarter of 2026 was $4.4 million, a decrease of $1.4 million, or 23.8%, from the second quarter of 2026, primarily due to lower gain on sale of SBA loans and other income attributable to a decline in the fair value of the equity securities, reflecting changes in market interest rates during the quarter, offset by an increase in SBA servicing income, net and other service charges, commissions and fees.  SBA loan sales totaled $9.7 million (sales premium of 8.16%) during the third quarter of 2026 compared to $27.1 million (sales premium of 8.21%) during the second quarter of 2026. Mortgage loan originations totaled $85.1 million during the third quarter of 2026 compared to $75.4 million during the second quarter of 2026. There were no mortgage loan sales during the third quarter of 2026 or the second quarter of 2026.  During the third quarter of 2026, the fair value of our SBA servicing asset decreased by $218,000 compared to a decrease in fair value of $86,000 during the second quarter of 2026. We also recorded no fair value impairment change on our mortgage servicing asset during the third quarter of 2026 or the second quarter of 2026. The unrealized losses recognized on our equity securities of $743,000.  These equity securities consist of the Company's investment in a mutual fund holding high-quality fixed income securities, which supports affordable housing in the Company's markets and qualifies under the Community Reinvestment Act. Under GAAP, changes in the fair value of this investment are recognized in earnings, even though the underlying holdings are bonds. This investment remains an important part of the Bank's community development strategy, particularly following the completion of our recent merger.

Compared to the third quarter of 2025, noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by $1.8 million or 29.0%, primarily due decreases in servicing income and gain on sale from our residential mortgage loans, servicing income from our SBA loans, other service charges and decline in fair value of equity securities included in other income, offset by increases in gains on sale on SBA loans and service charges on deposit accounts.

Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $16.5 million, a decrease of $871,000, or 5.0%, from the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to decreases in gain on sale and servicing income on residential mortgage loans, other service charges, and other income, offset by higher gains on sale and servicing income on SBA loans and service charges on deposit accounts.

Noninterest Expense

Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $20.0 million, an increase of $87,000, or 0.4%, from $20.0 million for the second quarter of 2026. This increase was primarily attributable to increases in salaries and employee benefits, advertising, occupancy and equipment, and data processing, partially offset by a decrease in merger-related expenses and other expenses.

Compared to the third quarter of 2025, noninterest expense during the third quarter of 2026 increased by $5.4 million, or 36.6%, primarily due to higher salaries and employee benefits, occupancy and equipment expense, data processing expense, security expense, loan expense, core deposit amortization expense, and merger-related expenses from the First IC acquisition that occurred in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $61.4 million, an increase of $18.9 million, or 44.3%, from $42.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was primarily attributable to increases in salaries and employee benefits partially due to higher commissions, employee insurance, and stock-based compensation, as well as higher expenses related to merger-related expenses, depreciation, occupancy, data processing, security, loans, and professional services.

The Company's efficiency ratio was 41.81% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 40.08% and 38.65% for the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively.

Income Tax Expense

The Company's effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 13.1%, compared to 27.7% for the second quarter of 2026 and 27.6% for the third quarter of 2025.  The decrease in effective income tax rate for the quarter was primarily driven by the utilization of tax credits during the current period.

Balance Sheet

The $77.9 million increase in total assets at September 30, 2026 compared to June 30, 2026 was primarily due to increases of $50.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and $36.4 million increase in other assets, primarily related increase in income taxes receivable resulting from the utilization of tax credits during the quarter. The increase in liabilities and equity was $72.7 million in deposits and $15.9 million in increase in retained earnings. data.title: S&P 500 closes lower to end rocky week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Telecom stocks down after report of SpaceX wireless carrier talks
  • S&P 500 energy sector climbs, tracking jump in oil prices
  • Investors turn focus to big earnings week, Fed meeting

By Lewis Krauskopf, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Ragini Mathur

The Dow Industrials and S&P 500 closed lower on Friday while technology shares steadied to end a turbulent week for the market-driving AI trade, and investors looked ahead to a busy slate of corporate earnings and a Federal Reserve interest-rate policy meeting.

Most S&P 500 sectors were weaker on Friday, including declines for the consumer staples and financial groups.

Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies report quarterly results, including Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon , three AI hyperscalers whose capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

"There is still fallout from the questioning of the AI trade," said Kristina Hooper, chief market strategist at Man Group. "There's certainly the potential that we see less invested in an AI data center build-out next year than has been projected. So I certainly think that's giving pause."

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 39.57 points, or 0.52%, to end at 7,623.86 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 55.17 points, or 0.21%, to 25,955.34. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 658.82 points, or 1.25%, to 52,209.16.

Telecommunications stocks fell, weighing on the communication services sector, after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier.

The energy sector rose, hitting a record high. Brent crude hit its highest level since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

Data from the University of Michigan showed US consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October, as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with robust corporate profit growth underpinning gains for major equity indexes this year. S&P 500 companies are on track to have increased earnings by more than 32% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.

The Fed is expected to keep interest rates steady when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, but investors will be eager for clues about whether the US central bank will hike rates at its December meeting. Wall Street is also increasingly focused on the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress.

data.title: Texas AG Sues OpenAI, Claiming ChatGPT Harmed Users
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging the company's chatbot ChatGPT had negative effects on consumers.

The suit claims OpenAI's large-language models lack adequate safeguards and can generate inaccurate or harmful information without disclosing the risk to users.

Paxton alleged that OpenAI's chatbots aided and abetted mass shooters, encouraged suicide, eroded critical thinking skills in individuals and was addictive for minors.

The claims are being brought under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices-Consumer Protection Act, alleging OpenAI deceived users about risk. The suit also alleges that OpenAI's operations violate the Securing Children Online through Parental Empowerment Act.

Paxton's suit seeks more than $1 million in monetary relief from OpenAI and is looking for the court to order the company to stop the allegedly harmful practices. Texas also seeks to hold Chief Executive Sam Altman "personally liable" for the alleged harm he has caused citizens, the suit says.

OpenAI could not immediately be reached for comment.
